title: Restricted options schema (meta-schema)
description: A META-schema: instances validated against this document are themselves JSON Schemas, namely the declarative description of the per-invocation options a host's own confirmation UI renders for one extension point. Hosts render publisher-supplied option metadata as ESCAPED PLAIN TEXT and must be able to bound the cost of rendering and validating it, so only a small, closed subset of JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 is accepted. Everything outside that subset — $ref/$defs, oneOf/anyOf/allOf/not, if/then/else, pattern/patternProperties, unevaluatedProperties, nested objects, and any format keyword — is rejected outright rather than ignored, so that a host and a plugin can never disagree about what a declaration means. Options are per-invocation USER input: they are never a place to carry credentials, and they never widen what data leaves the host (a declaration whose selected value would widen egress, retention, or data categories must be disclosed at its widest possible value in data_handling instead).

type.description: The options document is always a flat object; a top-level array or scalar has no rendering in a form UI.

additionalProperties.description: Closed-world is mandatory: a host validates submitted option values against this declaration and rejects unknown keys, so an open declaration would make that check vacuous.

required.description: Names of options the user must supply. Every entry is expected to also appear in properties; that cross-reference is a host-side check, not something this meta-schema can express.

properties.description: At most 20 fields. The cap is deliberate: an options form is a confirmation dialog, not a configuration console.

optionName.description: Identifier-shaped option key: conservative enough to be safe as an object key, a form control name, and a log field name at the same time.
optionName.$comment: The trailing negative lookahead is an ECMA-262-compatible exact end-of-input assertion.

plainText64.description: Short human-readable label. Rendered as escaped plain text; markup is never interpreted.

plainText300.description: Human-readable help text. Rendered as escaped plain text; markup is never interpreted.

scalar.description: Any single scalar value permitted as a default or enum member. Null is excluded: an absent option is expressed by omitting it, not by a null sentinel.

widget.description: Requested form control. A host MAY ignore the hint and fall back to the control implied by the field's type; it never loads a remote or publisher-supplied component.

uiHint.description: The only extension keyword permitted anywhere in an options schema, namespaced to the host platform ('x-contenttree-ui'). Custom widgets, remote option sources, and HTML labels are all deliberately unavailable.

type.description: Object-typed fields are absent by design: nesting depth is capped at 2 (this field, plus array items), which keeps both the rendered form and the server-side validator bounded.

optionField.description: One declared option. The keyword set is an allowlist: pattern, format, $ref, oneOf/anyOf/allOf/not, if/then/else and every other keyword are rejected by additionalProperties: false rather than silently ignored.

type.description: Array items are scalars only: arrays of objects or arrays of arrays are outside the subset.
